subject: Marketplace addendum — usage metering & revenue-share redlines
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@cloudshade.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudShade Legal <legal@cloudshade.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace addendum — initial redlines on metering and rev-share

Rishi,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — good discussion. Our legal team circulated an early set of redlines to the marketplace addendum and I wanted to put them on your radar. The main points are:

- Metering window: CloudShade wants a 90-day billing lookback for usage reconciliation; your standard is 30 days.
- Revenue-share calculation: prefer net-of-discounts on list price; Redwood's draft currently ties to gross reported billings.
- Audit and access: CloudShade requests quarterly audit rights and access to per-customer meter reports.
- Pass-through taxes: need explicit carveouts for VAT/GST in EU/UK.

I've attached the redlined Word doc for your team (CloudShade_Marketplace_Addendum_v2_redlines.docx). Can you confirm whether any of these are deal-breakers? If so, let's flag them and we can set a call with Kimberly and Karthik from your side.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
CloudShade Inc.

---
Attachment: CloudShade_Marketplace_Addendum_v2_redlines.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 42 KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@cloudshade.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace addendum — initial redlines on metering and rev-share

Marcus — thanks for sending this over and for the clear summary. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Karthik (partnerships ops) to triage. Quick thoughts from product/ops perspective:

- Metering window: 30 days is what our billing pipeline supports for automatic reconciliation and refund/credit issuance. Extending to 90 days materially increases exposure to retroactive adjustments and risk to our settlement engine.

- Rev-share base: we generally invoice and report gross billings less explicit discounts applied at the platform level (promo codes, marketplace coupons). We can consider a net-of-customer-discount position but need examples of discounts you typically see.

- Audit rights: we are open to limited audit rights (e.g., one remote audit per year with redacted PII). Quarterly full-access audits will be operationally heavy.

- VAT/GST: we already carve out taxes for jurisdictions in our order forms; if CloudShade needs explicit EU/UK language, Kimberly can propose text.

I've attached a short spreadsheet (redwood_metering_calcs.xlsx) that models the rev-share impact across different metering windows — helps quantify the delta. Can we aim for a 30–60 day compromise on the metering lookback, combined with a one-year audit right and narrower scope? If CloudShade can accept those guardrails, we can update the addendum and fast-track signature.

Call options: Tue 6/22 10:00 PT or Wed 6/23 09:00 PT. Which works?

- Rishi
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: redwood_metering_calcs.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 18 KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@cloudshade.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace addendum — initial redlines on metering and rev-share

Marcus / team — thanks for the redlines and the context. I reviewed CloudShade's annotations and attached proposed language that addresses: metering window, revenue definition, audit scope, and taxes. High level:

1) Metering window: propose compromise language — 60-day reconciliation period for billing adjustments. After 60 days, corrections are allowed only for processing errors or clear double-counting, with a 12-month overall cut-off for material corrections tied to fraud or system error.

2) Revenue definition: we will accept "net of marketplace service fees and refunds" but cannot accept exclusions for customer-level discounts applied directly by the seller unless documented. We propose a definition table with examples (see attached redline).

3) Audit: agree to annual remote audit with up to 10 business days' notice. Any on-site or more frequent audit requests will require mutual agreement and will be scoped to billing accuracy only (no access to customer content).

4) Taxes: provide explicit VAT/GST pass-through language for EU/UK; Redwood remains responsible for its own taxes but will pass-through collected marketplace levies to CloudShade where applicable.

Please see the attached redline: Redwood_responds_marketplace_addendum_v1.docx. Also added a HubSpot link to the deal for contract tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/HS-45278.

If CloudShade is comfortable with the 60-day window and sample revenue table, we can update the order form and route for signature this week. If not, please highlight the specific lines you need changed prior to the call.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: Redwood_responds_marketplace_addendum_v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 29 KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@cloudshade.com>
To: Kimberly Park <legal@cloudshade.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace addendum — initial redlines on metering and rev-share

Kimberly / Rishi — appreciate the thoughtful reply and the spreadsheet. Quick note after an internal read:

- We can accept the 60-day compromise on metering provided CloudShade retains the right to raise adjustments within 12 months for clear processing errors (your 12-month cut-off is acceptable in that context).
- Revenue definition: we'll sign up to the "net of marketplace service fees and refunds" wording but need two examples added to the table indicating how promotional credits applied by CloudShade's sales teams will be treated.
- Audit: quarterly audits are off the table for us too — annual remote audit with the 10-day notice is workable. We do want a limited right to request an additional audit in cases of suspected material discrepancy (to be mutually agreed).
- Taxes: EU VAT carveouts are fine; can you confirm whether Redwood will provide VAT invoices to CloudShade for pass-through charges?

Let's take the call today at 4:00 PT if that works for your side — I can have our marketplace ops join. If we get verbal alignment, we can exchange an updated doc and aim to finalize before the end of the week.

Best,
Marcus
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
CloudShade Inc.
